summary: The new URLENCODE_SAFE set leaves '+' unescaped despite the comment saying it is escaped, so literal plus signs in param values will be decoded as spaces by servers.

findings.explanation: The safe set is built from 0x20-0x7E minus (space, ", #, %, &, <, =, >) but does not exclude 0x2B ('+'). The comment says '+' is additionally escaped, yet urlencode(..., safe=URLENCODE_SAFE) will emit a literal '+' for a '+' in a value, while spaces are now also emitted as '+'. Params like {'q': 'a+b'} become indistinguishable from 'a b', corrupting data.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 0x2B to the exclusion list so '+' is encoded as %2B.

findings.explanation: No test covers a literal '+' (or other reserved characters) in param values, which would have caught the escaping gap above.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test such as params={'a': 'b+c'} expecting 'a=b%2Bc'.
